name: Leavitt’s variable-star period–brightness relation
description: Henrietta Leavitt found that brighter Magellanic Cloud variable stars have longer periods, a relationship later calibrated for astronomical distances.

impact.note: Once calibrated, it let astronomers measure distances beyond the Milky Way; the extragalactic distance scale, and Hubble's work, were built on it.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Leavitt noted the period–brightness pattern among 16 variables in her 1908 publication.

evidence.supports: Harvard dates Leavitt’s initial period–brightness observation to the 1908 list of 16 variables.
The Harvard 1912 circular attributes its preparation to Leavitt and lists 25 variable-star periods.
The 1908 report refers to sixteen variables and the brightness–period pattern.

caveats: The 1908 relation was a preliminary observation in one group of stars. Absolute calibration came later; the 1912 circular expanded the sample and was not the first statement. The 1908 paper says sixteen variables; the 1912 circular retrospectively refers to seventeen earlier periods. This discrepancy is unresolved.
